name: Do a proper handstand against a wall
blurb: Not a banana-shaped kick-up, but a straight, stacked line: hands, shoulders, hips, heels. Getting the shape right against a wall is what makes a free handstand possible later.
steps: Build the prerequisites: wrist prep every session, plus overhead shoulder mobility — most people cannot get their arms fully overhead without arching the back.
Learn the chest-to-wall version, walking your feet up the wall until your body is vertical and your chest is close to it. This forces the correct shape; the back-to-wall version lets you cheat.
Fix the shape: push tall through the shoulders, ribs down, glutes squeezed, legs together, toes pointed.
Hold for 20 seconds, then work up to a minute in accumulating sets.
Practise fingertip pressure: gripping the floor with your fingers is how you will balance later.
Learn to bail safely — a cartwheel exit — before you need it.
tips: Arched back with the belly out is the near-universal fault, and it will block progress to a free handstand.
Do a little every day. Handstands respond to frequency, not to long punishing sessions.
Warm your wrists properly. Wrist pain is the main reason people quit.
proof: A 60-second chest-to-wall handstand with a straight line and no sagging.
